scope: Complete implemented scheduling controls: original task attributes, cross-task/group/UID selection and permissions, migration completion, direct on-demand CPU-pool startup, original identity through fork/exec/exit and source seccomp. No second subsystem migration.
build_configuration: Mac release Dev with TRAMES_MOLTENVK_STATIC_DIR pointing to the existing verified macOS arm64 archive, Xcode/SDK 27.2. No driver or guest library sources changed.
concurrency: Original IoTask atomics own affinity/nice/policy; self queries avoid the PID index. Existing PID directory provides original cross-task/group/UID identities.

The same group-control lock serializes actual mask publication and execution entry. Only an original running target must depart before accepted migration completion; caller waits return the execution slot.
Original completion events retain pending migrations across rekey/exit and cohort handoff; callbacks run after resource locks. No numeric PID relookup or syscall replay.

The queue can start a required cold original executor through the shared CPU pool. Per-slot startup/control locks do not cover guest execution; no service thread, polling bus or eager all-CPU startup is added.
Birth, process-group/session mutation, credentials and exec publish authority at actual write boundaries. Ordinary owner queries do not rebuild every task projection.
Ordinary fields use relaxed atomics; completion has actual release/acquire synchronization. No new guest memory fences, algorithm-wide/native locks, unsafe impls or host scheduling changes.

native_linux.model: Native ARM64 Linux ABI in the existing local VZ CI environment, not a macOS-native affinity API.

benchmark.method: Four threads x 256 loops x four scheduling calls. Two warmups per mode/binary/CPU count, five counterbalanced unprofiled pairs. Longest worker duration excludes pthread setup/join; host process wall is also retained. Metrics run separately. Existing desktop/stable sessions remain; all builds, tests and local Linux CI ended before these Mac timings. No samplers, tracing or window capture. Native Linux uses the exact static ELF in the six-vCPU local CI environment and is contextual; macOS has no equivalent Linux affinity syscall ABI.

background_before_benchmark.note: One instantaneous pre-run snapshot, not whole-run utilization accounting; system process names and PIDs are retained only in ignored local evidence.

remaining_boundaries: Traced calls and actual seccomp signal/termination effects keep their owner task-policy boundary.
sched_rr_get_interval and sched_setattr/getattr remain ENOSYS, now completed on continuous workers; realtime/deadline policies are not newly implemented.
Single-CPU/solo execution retains its coordinated caller path; it has no additional syscall RPC.

Dynamic proc/sys and special paths, namespace/credential administration, structural VM publication, legacy nonmember adoption, embedding control and generic unhandled dispatch remain as listed in the shared inventory.
Only the final control ioctl remains in these whole-session diagnostics. Zero service requests alone does not prove coordinator removal: baseline service requests were already zero.
measurement_limits: These are scheduling-control loops, not Firefox, Geekbench or general application speedups. Longest-worker loop and whole-process wall are separate measurements.
Existing stable/desktop services remained active. Native ARM Linux is an exact-ELF contextual reference in the six-vCPU local CI environment; macOS has no equivalent Linux affinity syscall ABI.
The former cold-CPU prototype timed out because owner-only slot startup remained. Source-started slots fix that dependency; the preserved timeout log is not a before/after performance sample.
An initial test build omitted the static Vulkan library flag; the matched baseline passed, and the final exact measured/installed binary passed GPU/video with the reused verified archive.

Self-update timing reapplies the allowed full mask, SCHED_OTHER/zero parameter and nice 7; it is not a continuous CPU-migration timing. Actual migration and cold-slot behavior are validated separately.
